facts.text: Lifetime first aired Stalked by My Doctor on December 26, 2015, the day after Christmas, as counter-programming to its holiday movies.
The film is not based on a true story, per Bustle. Real doctor-stalker cases exist, like UK patient Raymond Knight, jailed for harassing his GP, but their details don't match.
Eric Roberts (Dr. Beck) earned an Oscar nomination for Runaway Train (1985) and was in The Dark Knight (2008). Here he plays a TV doctor who is also, apparently, a stalker.
Eric Roberts is the older brother of Julia Roberts. They made just one movie together, Blood Red (1989).
Eric Roberts acted in 74 films in 2017 alone and has over 700 credits, making him one of the most prolific English-speaking screen actors.
Eric Roberts is the only non-British actor to play the Master in Doctor Who (the 1996 TV movie), and the only actor to be a villain in both the Batman and Doctor Who franchises.
Dr. Albert Beck, played by Eric Roberts, was named among TV Guide's 50 most memorable villains in its July 15, 2016 issue.
TMDB lists the film's budget at $4 million, which would be hefty for a Lifetime thriller.
Dr. Beck's 'I am un-friending you!' rant at his online date is a modern twist: the film opens with him being dumped after meeting her through a dating website.
Tara Malenfant made her screen debut in this film, according to IMDb.
Lisa Marie Bowman of Unobtainium13 called Eric Roberts' Dr. Beck 'creepy in a good way', citing his too-quick smiles, leaning in too close and childlike outbursts.
Goof spotted by viewers: Dr. Beck is a cardiologist, but cardiologists generally don't do open-heart surgery. Cardiac surgeons do that, and cardiologists only implant devices like pacemakers.
Viewers noticed Dr. Beck rubs ointment on Sophie's chest and preps for surgery without ever wearing medical gloves.
Jon Briddell (Sophie's dad, Jim Green) also supplied the voice of K.I.T.T., the talking car, on NBC's Knight Rider series.
Before the premiere, Bustle's preview misnamed Eric Roberts' villain as 'Doctor Grey.' In the film he is cardiologist Dr. Albert Beck.
Jon Briddell met his wife Michelle while working on a dinner-theater show that toured for the USO. They hooked up at a NATO base in Sarajevo.
Writer-director Doug Campbell's earlier Lifetime thrillers include Sugar Daddies, Stalked By My Neighbor, Betrayed at 17 and The Cheating Pact, per blogger Lisa Marie Bowman.
Ryan's text from Dr. Beck reads 'Bride of Frankenstein', a nod to the 1935 James Whale classic that the film references.
In a 2020 UPI interview, Eric Roberts said he plays 'a very bad doctor' in the series, loves the project, and called it 'so much fun to do.'
Eric Roberts has said he quit drinking in 1995. A 1981 car crash in Connecticut, in which he crashed his jeep into a tree, left him in a coma for 72 hours.
Eric Roberts said he turned to B movies when 'the big starring roles stopped coming.' For Sharktopus, Roger Corman let him bring any guests he wanted to a month-long shoot at a Mexican resort.
Eric Roberts' daughter, Emma Roberts, was born February 10, 1991. His ring finger is also permanently disfigured from a 1980s car accident.
The 2015 film's popularity with fans led to a series. After the third film, a fan started a Change.org petition and a Twitter account asking for a fourth Stalked by My Doctor movie, per Bustle.
Lifetime's takeaway, per reviewers: a spectrum review calls this first film the strongest of the series, mainly for a memorable freak-out scene by Eric Roberts' Dr. Beck.
Spectrum Culture says the 2018 sequel Patient's Revenge gives Eric Roberts a dual role: Dr. Beck and his own conscience. Part four, A Sleepwalker's Nightmare, was written and directed by Jeff Hare.
Dr. Beck survived to return in Stalked by My Doctor: The Return (2016), Patient's Revenge (2018), A Sleepwalker's Nightmare (2019), and Just What the Doctor Ordered (2021).
Bustle's preview said the trailer showed syringes used both inside and outside the operating room, and sold the film as a gritty thriller, not a true story.
Writer-director Doug Campbell also made the sequel The Return. The Spectrum Culture review notes he made about 15 TV features in five years.
Trivia: Brianna Joy Chomer (Sophie Green) knocks out Eric Roberts with four golf-club strokes in this film. In A Dangerous Date (2018) she is slapped three times by Jillian Murray.
Spectrum Culture praised the series' star: Eric Roberts 'smokes, glazes and carves' his material 'with voracious gusto' as Dr. Albert Beck, the role he plays in every film of the franchise.
